content: 1. An analysis was conducted to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of carbetocin for the prevention of hemorrhage following cesarean delivery in Ecuador, as published in the Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research in 2017 (Volume 12, Issue 9). 2. Voon HY, Shafie AA, Bujang MA, and Suharjono HN performed a cost-effectiveness analysis of carbetocin use during cesarean sections in a high-volume maternity unit. Their findings were published in the Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology Research in 2018 (Volume 44, Issue 1, Pages 109–116). 3. Van der Nelson HA, Draycott T, Siassakos D, Yau CWH, and Hatswell AJ conducted an economic impact analysis comparing carbetocin and oxytocin for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage during cesarean sections in the United Kingdom. This study was published in the European Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology and Reproductive Biology in 2017 (Volume 210, Pages 286–291). 4. Luni Y, Borakati A, Matah A, Skeats K, and Eedarapalli P carried out a prospective cohort study to assess the cost-effectiveness of carbetocin in preventing postpartum hemorrhage during cesarean sections. Their research appeared in the Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 2017 (Volume 37, Issue 5, Pages 601–604). 5. Caceda SI, Ramos RR, and Saborido CM conducted a pharmacoeconomic study comparing carbetocin and oxytocin for the prevention of hemorrhage following cesarean delivery in Lima, Peru. This study was published in the Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research in 2018 (Volume 7, Issue 1, Pages 49–55). 6. Higgins L, Mechery J, and Tomlinson AJ explored whether carbetocin provides clinical or financial benefits compared to oxytocin for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage during cesarean sections. Their findings were presented in a structured abstract published in the Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 2011 (Volume 31, Issue 8, Pages 732–739). 7. The Joint Formulary Committee included information on carbetocin in the British National Formulary 72 (September 2016–March 2017), published in London, United Kingdom, in 2017. 8. Lang DL, Zhao FL, and Robertson J analyzed the cost consequences of using misoprostol for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage in low-resource settings. Their study was published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2015 (Volume 15, Issue 1, Article 305). 9. The One Health Tool provided draft intervention assumptions in January 2016, which were accessed on November 8, 2018. 10. The report titled State of Inequality: Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health was accessed on November 5, 2018, via the World Health Organization's online repository.
